Questions

Questions people ask

Answers about bookings and the member area. For questions about treatment itself, it’s best to ask the clinic directly.

All questions
Where can I see my remaining sessions?

Sign in and open “My treatments”. Each package shows remaining, reserved and available sessions, with its history.

If I buy on GoWabi, is my appointment booked?

No. Buying a GoWabi voucher is not an appointment. After buying, book a time with the clinic, which checks the voucher through the merchant process before your visit.

Can I change the language of Bella’s messages?

Yes, in Preferences. Screen language and message language are separate: changing the website language does not change your messages automatically.

What is the difference between “remaining” and “available”?

“Remaining” is every unused session, including any already reserved for an upcoming appointment. “Available” is what you can still book. For example: 4 remaining with 1 reserved means 3 available to book.

Questions people ask

Where can I see my remaining sessions?

Sign in and open “My treatments”. Each package shows remaining, reserved and available sessions, with its history.

If I buy on GoWabi, is my appointment booked?

No. Buying a GoWabi voucher is not an appointment. After buying, book a time with the clinic, which checks the voucher through the merchant process before your visit.

Can I change the language of Bella’s messages?

Yes, in Preferences. Screen language and message language are separate: changing the website language does not change your messages automatically.

What is the difference between “remaining” and “available”?

“Remaining” is every unused session, including any already reserved for an upcoming appointment. “Available” is what you can still book. For example: 4 remaining with 1 reserved means 3 available to book.

You can cancel at no charge until the time shown in “In short” above, in the member area or through the team. Cancelling a request that hasn’t been confirmed simply withdraws it.

  • Booking from a package sets one session aside for that appointment. It is used only once the treatment is done.
  • If you cancel, the session becomes available again; if you move the appointment, the session moves with it.
  • The appointment must fall on or before the validity date shown in your account.

01Our aim

We design and build to WCAG 2.2 level AA. The website has not been fully audited against it, so we don’t claim that it meets every criterion.

02What is built in

  • Pages work with a keyboard, with a skip link to the main content and a visible focus outline.
  • The main text and background colours are checked against the AA contrast ratio.
  • Images that carry meaning have text alternatives.
  • Every page declares its language (Thai, English or Chinese).
  • If your device asks for reduced motion, the website turns its animations off.

03Known limits

  • The map is a Google Maps frame, which we cannot adapt. The address is also given as text.
  • The route video has no sound or captions. The Visit page gives the same route as written steps.
  • The route shown on the Visit page includes stairs, and step-free access is not yet confirmed. If stairs are difficult for you, please contact the team before you come.
  • Social media posts and GoWabi open on other websites, which handle accessibility in their own way.

Getting here

04Report a problem

We check with automated tests (axe), a colour-contrast check and keyboard use. If you use a screen reader or other assistive technology and something doesn’t work, or you need information in another form, please tell the team by LINE or phone.

Before your first consultation

A consultation is time to talk things through and ask everything you want to. You don’t need to know in advance which treatment suits you.

Topic
Preparing
Reading time
2 min
Last updated

What to bring

These details help the assessment fit you. A note on your phone is enough.

  • The medicines, supplements and skin products you use
  • Any allergies, including to medicines, anaesthetics or products
  • Aesthetic treatments you’ve had recently, and when
  • Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any condition you’re being treated for

What to ask

  • What the treatment does, and how many sessions it usually takes
  • The possible side effects and risks
  • How to look after yourself afterwards
  • How it’s priced, and what the price includes
  • Whether there are alternatives, including not treating at all

Afterwards

If you’re unsure, give yourself time to think it over. A treatment can be booked later, online or through the team.

Wherever you go, a few questions help you understand what you’re agreeing to before you decide.

Topic
Before you decide
Reading time

Who performs it

Ask who will carry out the treatment and what their qualifications are. A medical procedure should be performed by a licensed doctor.

You can check a doctor’s licence yourself: search the register on the Medical Council of Thailand’s website.

The Medical Council of Thailand (opens in a new tab)

The product or device

Ask which product or device will be used, and whether it is approved by Thailand’s Food and Drug Administration. You can ask to see the packaging before you start.

Aftercare

  • What is common afterwards, and how long it usually lasts
  • What to avoid in the first days
  • Who to contact if something seems wrong, and how

How it’s priced

Ask what the price includes, how many sessions are usually needed, and whether follow-up visits cost extra. On this site, each treatment page shows how it’s priced.

Choose “Report a balance issue” on the package page, or contact the team by LINE or phone.
